title: Bond Parameters Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Two magnets snap to one exact gap, a folding chair opens to one fixed angle, and a rope is harder to snap than a thread. Every chemical bond has a gap, an angle and a strength too. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we measure a bond like an engineer.

On the molecule bench, two oxygen atoms share one pair, then two, and a live ruler drops from 148 pm to 121 pm. Energy bars grow for H2 (435.8), O2 (498) and N2 (946 kJ/mol) as bond order rises. We build covalent and van der Waals radii from H2, show the 104.5 degree angle in water, meet isoelectronic N2, CO and NO+, and work out the average O-H bond enthalpy in water (464.5 kJ/mol). Then an exam trap, an original exam pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 43 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Gap, angle, strength
0:28 The four bond parameters
1:04 Bond length and bond order on the bench
1:26 Bond enthalpy: H2, O2, N2
1:53 Pause and think
2:07 Covalent and van der Waals radius
2:40 Bond angle and isoelectronic molecules
3:03 Worked example: average O-H enthalpy
3:35 Exam trap
3:58 Practice question (JEE Main / NEET pattern)
4:42 Recap and three questions
